# Pending changes (since patch 0023, 2026-11-25)

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: a tab of its own in the mesh editor

**Asked:** study a curve-and-solid CAD-style modeling app's tools, reproduce the most intuitive ones in
the mesh editor, in a separate tab "Curve modeling" (so the GUI doesn't get busy), with tabs in the
right-click menu too; work well with the existing editor, test thoroughly, update the docs.

**Done:**
- **Tabs.** The right panel is now a TabContainer: **Mesh** (everything it had) and **Curve modeling**.
  The right-click menu has the same two tabs (a TabBar over two pages, built by the new `_menu_page`);
  it opens on the one used last (Curve modeling while curves are picked). `show_right_tab(i)`,
  `curve_tab_shown()`.
- **Curves** (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, a node of the editor like deform_tools / mesh_ops):
  line (polyline, per-corner fillet radii kept on it), spline (centripetal Catmull-Rom through its
  points), circle, three-point arc, bezier (bridges). Model-space control points + plane normal; drawn
  over the view by an overlay Control (blue; picked amber with point handles), redrawn only when the
  camera moves.
- **Sketching** on a **construction plane**: Auto (the part's surface under the first click - a curve
  drawn on a face - else the ground), Ground / Front / Side / View / Selection (selected faces' best
  plane, or the picked curve's). Snapping to the plane's grid (step 0.05 m) and to curve points, ends,
  side middles, circle centres and parts' corners (Ctrl: free); a coloured ring shows what it caught.
  Tools: Line L, Spline P, Circle C, Arc Shift+C, Rectangle Shift+R (Alt: from centre), Polygon Shift+P
  (wheel / + -: sides). Typed sizes (length, radius, "w h") + Enter. Click the first point to close;
  Enter / right-click / double click ends; Backspace takes a point back; the tool stays on; Esc stops.
- **Editing:** click to pick (Shift: more), drag points (snapped), drag a curve to move it in its plane;
  delete, duplicate, mirror (X), radial array (6 round Y), offset (mitred; interactive), fillet corners
  (interactive radius, kept on the curve), join, bridge (G1 bezier between nearest ends), reverse,
  close/open. Every change one undo step (edit mode: on its own stack).
- **Solids from curves** (each a new part, one undo step; closed outlines -> closed solids facing out, so
  booleans work): Extrude (mouse along the normal with a live preview, grid-snapped, or typed),
  Revolve (about a picked two-point line, else the model's Y; mouse/typed angle), Loft (picked order;
  loops lined up and wound the same way), Sweep (profile along path, rotation-minimising frames),
  Pipe (round tube; mouse/typed radius), Fill (flat faces). Built with Shapes.B sheets/caps (creases at
  sharp corners, smooth elsewhere), turned outward by the signed volume.
- **On the mesh** group in the tab: Push / pull faces, Fillet edges (the mesh_ops fillet), Inset, Flatten.
- **Saved with the model**: `<model file>.curves.json` beside the written glb (in the override's
  variant; removed when there are no curves); read back on open via `_read_source`.
- 20 new icons (m_cv_*) in their own file scripts/editor/mesh/curve_icons.gd (EditorIcons.layers_of
  hands m_cv_* to it).
- Docs: data/docs/editor.md - the intro's tabs; new sections mesh-curves, mesh-curves-plane,
  mesh-curves-edit, mesh-curves-solids; saving mentions the curves file.

**Numbers:** 6 sketch tools, 6 construction planes, 10 curve edits, 6 solid makers; tests
tests/test_curve_modeling.gd - 6 tests (shapes; offset/join/bridge; 13 solids checked closed + facing out
+ volume within 1-3%: e.g. extruded 1 x 0.5 x 0.2 = 0.1 m3, revolved square torus 2piRA, lofted circles
= a cylinder, pipe pi r^2 L; tabs + menu + tooltips; sketch by clicks with grid snap, typed radius,
undo/redo, pick, extrude part + undo, typed extrude, fillet corners, offset; keys per tab; saving).
Mesh tests 78/78, editor 35/35, tooltips 9/9, fonts 3/3 still pass.

**Files:** new scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/curve_icons.gd,
tests/test_curve_modeling.gd; changed scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (tabs, menu pages, hooks: view input,
keys, open/save, undo, _update_ui), scripts/editor/editor_icons.gd (m_cv_* hand-off), data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-25 - Mesh editor: Fillet (Ctrl+B)
Asked: an edge fillet (rounded bevel) in the mesh editor's edit mode - selected edges (or the selected faces' border) rounded into strips of quads, a width and a number of segments, corners closed, the mesh kept closed; segments 1 a chamfer.
Done:
- `scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_bevel.gd` (new): `MeshBevel.fillet(em, edge_ids, width, segments)` and `usable_edges(em, ids)`. Each corner of a face at a filleted edge's end moves in (both sides filleted: in from each by the width; one side: slid along the other side until the width from it - the faces either side of that side meet halfway). Each edge becomes `segments` rows of quads across, its profile a rational-quadratic arc (a circle's arc) tangent to both faces. Corners: one edge ending - its arc joins the face across the end when it lies flat in it (a box: the end faces get the rounded corner), else a face of its own; two edges with nothing between - their arcs welded (a mitre); three or more - a fan whose middle is pushed out to the ball rounding the corner. Faces round the ends rebuilt from their outlines (ear clipping; UVs / colours / bone weights blended from the old corners, shared across seamless sides); the rest keep their triangles. The width is held below where corners would pass each other (thin triangles at a sphere's pole). Every new point = old point + offset x width.
- `scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_ops.gd`: `begin_fillet()` (Ctrl+B through `key()`; the EDIT MESH row and the right-click menu): the mouse away from the middle widens it (starts at 10% of the edges' mean length), typed digits set the width, the wheel or + / - the segments (4 to start, then the last used; 1-32); remade from the snapshot whenever they change; click / Enter keeps (one undo step, the strips selected), right-click / Esc cancels. `fillet_width()`, `set_fillet_segments()`, `fillet_segments`.
- `scripts/editor/editor_icons.gd`: the `m_fillet` icon (a block's rounded corner, the strip's rows, the old corner faint).
- `data/docs/editor.md`: a Fillet section (mesh-fillet) before Loop cut.
- `tests/test_mesh_bevel.gd` (new, 6 tests): a box's one edge (8 -> 16 points, 6 -> 10 faces, closed, the arc's points 0.1 from its centre line), a chamfer (10 points, 7 faces, volume exactly 1 - 0.1²/2), all 12 edges (104 points, 150 faces; chamfered: 24 points, 26 faces), two / four / three edges at corners, the interactive tool (typed width, - / wheel segments, undo, cancel, face mode), a cylinder's rim, a whole sphere and torus staying closed.
Numbers: a box all round at segments 4: 8 -> 104 points, 6 -> 150 faces; a sphere's 600 edges: ~130 ms, a torus's 576: ~95 ms (remade on each width change while dragging).
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_bevel.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_ops.gd, scripts/editor/editor_icons.gd, data/docs/editor.md, tests/test_mesh_bevel.gd (new).
- (Curve modeling, after the fillet landed) The tab's "On the mesh" group calls mesh_ops.begin_fillet. Full
  suite 252/252. fps_test talos: mesh editor tour 493 FPS (it was ~450 before this change - fresh previews
  made at the start of the tour; known), rail switching 804 avg / p95 3.7 ms. The curve overlay redraws only
  when the camera moves and curves exist.

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: procedural solids that follow their curves, and holes

**Asked:** the solids made with the curve tools should always be procedurally generated and controlled
by their curves (as in the curve-and-solid modeling app the tab is modelled on).

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd):**
- Every curve has an id (`_next_id`; copies - duplicate, mirror, radial array, join, offset - get new
  ones; kept in <model>.curves.json; past every id a saved recipe names, on open).
- A solid keeps its **recipe** in its part's meta "curve_solid": {kind, ids, value, segs, axis} (`spec_of`
  for the picked curves; a revolve's two-point axis line by id). `solid_of(spec)` makes the mesh from the
  curves as they are now; `refresh_solids()` remakes every procedural part whose curves or recipe changed
  (compared by a key: the recipe + its curves as JSON; the material kept) - after every curve change, a
  point or curve drag (live), fillet / offset previews, undo / redo, a recipe change, a model opened.
  A part in edit mode, or whose curves are gone, is left as it is.
- **SOLID** box at the top of the tab for a procedural part: Height / Angle / Radius, a revolve's Steps
  (one undo step each, made again at once), **Pick its curves**, **Make plain mesh** (undoable).
- Unlinked (a plain mesh) when its mesh is edited in edit mode (mesh_editor._leave_edit, restored by
  undo), when it's a boolean's A (shape_tools, restored by undo), or by Make plain mesh. Duplicated parts
  keep the recipe: instances sharing the curves. The binding state keeps it too.
- Saved in the glb's extras as "atrapos_curves" (mesh_editor.write_to) and read back on open
  (mesh_editor._set_model), like the shape recipes.
- **Holes:** closed curves inside a closed curve in its plane are holes (`regions()` - nesting depth:
  odd = hole, even = outline / island); extrude and fill make the outline and its holes one cap
  (`keyhole()` joins each hole by a slit) triangulated by the editor's own ear clipping (`cap()`: the
  engine's triangulator put triangles inside the holes); hole walls face into the hole.
- `sample()` always returns a copy (callers turn loops round - a line's own points were at risk).
- Docs: data/docs/editor.md - new section mesh-curves-procedural; holes in mesh-curves-solids.

**Numbers:** tests/test_curve_modeling.gd now 8 tests - test_procedural_solids (widen the curve 1 -> 2 m:
volume 0.1 -> 0.2 m3; undo / redo; corners filleted on the curve round the solid; height 0.4 from the
SOLID box + undo; Pick its curves; duplicate follows; curve deleted -> stays; plain mesh stops
following while the linked copy follows; undo relinks; recipe through JSON), test_holes (round hole,
picked the other way and pushed down, two holes, hole with an island: all closed, volume within 1%;
fill ring area).

**Files:** scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/shape_tools.gd,
tests/test_curve_modeling.gd, data/docs/editor.md.
- (Procedural solids) The SOLID box's controls live in `_panel_btns` ("w_*", `_w()`), the next curve id in
  a meta (`_nid()`), built by `build_solid_box()` - no new member variables, so the change hot reloads into
  an open mesh editor. Full suite 254/254.

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: solids carry their curves, curve booleans, live solid booleans

**Asked:** (1) the user found solids "disconnected from their curves, floating above them" - the part
had been moved (a drag on the selected part moves it) while its curves stayed; (2) booleans with
curves - both 2D booleans of curves and booleans of solids that stay procedural.

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd):**
- **A solid's place is its curves' place.** `owner_xfs()`: each curve id -> the transform (in the model)
  of the first part made from it (a live boolean's B: A's times B's place in A). Curves are drawn,
  picked (`pick`, `pick_handle`), snapped to, dragged (handle: on its placed plane, back into its own
  space; whole curve: the move turned into its space) and used for the selection's plane where they're
  placed. Copies (duplicate, mirror, radial array, offset, join, bridge) are `baked()` - made where they
  show. A new solid from placed curves gets their placement (`add_part(..., place)`), the extrude /
  revolve / pipe drag and preview too. Curve points stay in the part's own space - moving a part needs
  no rewrite of its curves and undo of the move just works.
- **Curve booleans** (`curve_boolean(op)` / static `curve_bool(cs, op)`): union / subtract / intersect of
  the picked closed curves on one plane (Geometry2D.merge / clip / intersect_polygons in the plane's 2D
  coordinates; clockwise results are holes), tidied (no repeated or collinear points), replacing the
  picked curves as closed lines; refused when not coplanar. Buttons Union / Subtract / Intersect curves
  (icons m_union / m_difference / m_intersect) in the CURVES group and the menu.
- **Live booleans** (scripts/editor/mesh/shape_tools.gd `_bool_apply`): A and B both procedural and not a
  slice -> A's recipe becomes {kind: "bool", op, a: A's recipe, b: B's recipe, b_xf: B in A (`xf_arr`)};
  `solid_of` makes both and runs MeshBool.run at once; `spec_ids()` gathers every curve of a recipe
  (keys, Pick its curves, the SOLID box: "A live difference, made from N curves"). While a curve is
  dragged, a live boolean is made again at most every 120 ms (pending ones in `_process`). Each surface
  keeps its material on a remake. Undo restores A's own recipe.
- New state kept in metas (bool_at, solids_pending) - hot reloads into an open editor.
- Docs: mesh-curves-edit (curve booleans), mesh-curves-procedural (moving a solid moves its curves; live
  booleans).

**Numbers:** tests/test_curve_modeling.gd 11 tests - new: test_moved_solid_takes_its_curves (picked /
handle at the moved place, copy lands there, new solid placed with it), test_curve_booleans (squares
union 1.75 m2 with 8 corners, intersect 0.25, subtract 0.75, square minus inner circle -> outline + hole
-> extruded volume (1 - 0.04 pi) x 0.1, non-coplanar refused, editor replace + undo), test_live_boolean
(block minus cylinder; hole curve widened r 0.2 -> 0.3: volume follows; block widened: follows; B's curves
still placed; undo -> A's extrusion back).

**Files:** scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/shape_tools.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd,
data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-25 - Curve booleans: lean results, the path curve, Simplify curve

**Asked:** subtracting one curve from another made a new curve with a ton of unnecessary points (every
arc came back as the boolean's dense outline - ~60 points for a square with a round bite).

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd):**
- A new curve kind **path**: control points + per-point `sharp` flags - smooth through most (a
  Catmull-Rom run between corners), broken at the sharp ones; a run with no points between two
  corners is a straight side (`path_pts`). Saved (`sharp` in the JSON), reversed, closed / opened,
  offset like lines and splines.
- **`fit_path()`**: a dense outline as few points as keep its shape - corners (turns over 25°) and
  the ends of straight sides kept and marked sharp, a point every ~40° of turning along bends, a
  bare arc between two corners gets its middle. No bends: a plain line of corners.
- Curve boolean results: a curve that comes through whole (a hole inside, an untouched outline) is
  that curve itself (`_same_curve` - same area, every point on it: a circle stays a circle);
  the others fitted as paths / lines.
- Open splines' ends now carry on the bend of their last three points (quadratic extrapolation
  instead of a straight mirror): arcs stay round to their ends (paths' runs end at corners).
- **Simplify curve** (CURVES group + menu): the picked closed lines / paths with more points than
  needed fitted the same way, in place - their ids kept, so solids made from them follow; one undo step.
- Docs: mesh-curves-edit (lean results, Simplify curve).

**Numbers:** square minus a circle biting its side: 6 corners + arc points, <= 12 points (was ~40-60),
area within 1%; square minus a circle inside: 4-corner line + the circle itself; two circles unioned:
12 points (was 92), area within 1% of the exact lens formula. Tests: test_curve_boolean_results_are_lean,
test_simplify_curve (dense 40+ -> <= 12, id kept, its extrusion follows within 1.5%, undo).
- (Lean results, fixed) The user's case - a small circle minus a big one overlapping it - came out
  distorted near the cut: a short arc of the big circle (~45°) got its one point right at its end, and the
  spline sagged 6.6 cm off the true circle. Now: (1) each bend's points are spread evenly along its turning
  (~35° apart, at least its middle); (2) a bend whose points lie on one circle (the arcs a boolean of
  circles leaves - tolerance 0.4% of r: the boolean's corners sit on the outline's chords) is drawn as that
  exact arc (`_arc_run`: through its ends and middle point) and kept to its middle point alone; (3) a
  spline's open ends carry on the circle through their last three points (`_beyond`). The user's case:
  10 points / 6.6 cm off -> 4 points / under 1 mm off. Moving a path point off its circle: a 3-point run
  stays an arc through it, longer runs become splines through their points. Test
  test_curve_boolean_keeps_true_arcs (subtract / intersect / union of the user's circles: < 2 mm off,
  <= 14 points).
- (Lean results, intersect) Intersecting the user's circles (a small lens) gave 11 points, 10 of them
  corners: a side counted as straight when long next to the whole shape, and the lens is small next to
  the big circle's 10 cm sides. Now a side is straight when it runs corner to corner, is over 3x longer
  than the sides it joins smoothly (not across a corner - the boolean leaves 3 mm slivers there), or
  barely turns at either end. The lens: 4 points (2 corners + an arc's middle each), on the true
  circles. Test test_small_intersections_stay_lean (the lens both ways; a small square cut by a circle:
  <= 5 points).

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: move, turn and scale curves in 3D

**Asked:** "why can't I move curves in 3D space" - curves could only be dragged within their own plane.

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd):** `begin_xf(mode)` - with curves picked, **G** moves them over
the plane facing the view (or along X / Y / Z: `on_line`), **R** turns them about their middle (the line
of sight, or an axis; the way the mouse circles on screen), **S** scales them about their middle (or along
one axis); X / Y / Z toggle the axis; grid / 15° / 0.05 snapping (Ctrl: free); typed numbers (distance,
degrees, factor); click / Enter keeps, Esc / right-click cancels; one undo step. Applied through each
curve's placement (a curve placed by its moved solid turns where it shows: `_xf_apply`), its plane's
normal turned with it, fillet radii scaled with a uniform scale; the solids follow live. Buttons Move /
Turn / Scale curves (icons m_move / m_rotate / m_scale) in the CURVES group and the menu. While any curve
operation runs, X / Y / Z are taken (X no longer reaches the editor's Delete).
Docs: mesh-curves-edit ("In 3D").

**Numbers:** test_curves_move_turn_scale_in_3d - G Y 0.5: lifted, the extrusion follows; R X 90: plane
faces Z, the solid turned, same volume (0.1), closed; S 2: volume 0.4; undo x3 back; X while moving = axis;
Esc cancels. Mouse check: free drag 100 px up from a tilted view lifts 0.35 m (view plane); along Y 0.45 m;
turn about X 90°.

## 2026-11-25 - Curve booleans across planes

**Asked:** booleans with curves on different planes and offsets.

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd `curve_bool` / `curve_boolean`):** worked out on the first picked
curve's plane, the others projected onto it along its normal (its 2D coordinates already were a
projection; the "all on one plane" refusal is gone). On a parallel plane a curve lands as it is (a curve
coming through whole is returned flattened onto the plane: `_flat_copy` - a lifted circle stays a
circle); at an angle it's projected (a tilted circle -> an ellipse, made a lean path); edge-on
(`projectable()`: no area seen along the normal) it's left out. The note lists how many were brought down /
projected and which were left out. Docs: mesh-curves-edit.

**Numbers:** test_curve_booleans_across_planes - square minus a circle 0.3 m above: hole still a circle on
the square's plane, extruded (1 - 0.04 pi) x 0.1; minus a circle tilted 60°: an ellipse hole of area
pi r^2 cos 60° (within 2%); edge-on: not projectable, left out (the rest still done).
- (Curve modeling, fix) The user's panel showed every boolean button disabled with two curves picked: the
  panel kept each item's enabled-check and action as lambdas made when it was built, and a hot reload of
  curve_tools.gd leaves such lambdas invalid - stuck disabled, dead when pressed. Now the panel's buttons
  call `_run_item(name)` (a method, bound by name) and `_refresh_panel` works out every item's state from
  the items as they are now; the panel's spin boxes / check boxes connect to methods (`_spec_value`,
  `_set_snap_grid`...). No lambdas connected in the panel. Test test_panel_buttons_enable_and_run
  (off with one curve, on with two, pressing Union runs it, every pressed connection a method of the tools).

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: positive and negative solids; curves redrawn as their solid moves

**Asked:** an extruded solid can be a negative solid that live-subtracts from another solid; "positive
by default, or negative for subtractions". Also: moving a solid, its curves only showed in their new
place after a click.

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd):**
- Solids are positive by default. While extruding, **N** toggles negative: `_neg_target` finds the solid it
  cuts (`part_containing` - the extrusion's middle inside a part, by counting ray crossings of its skin -
  else `part_overlapping`, the most box overlap); the preview turns red; the hint names the target. On
  confirm the extrusion is made, then `cut_from` runs a difference with the target at once (shape_tools
  boolean, B not kept) - live when both are procedural (the target's recipe "it minus the cutter").
- SOLID box: **Negative** (`make_negative`: the selected solid cut from the solid it's in) and **Make the
  cut positive** (`make_positive`: on a solid whose recipe is a difference - back to its own recipe, the
  cutter a positive part of its own again where it was, still following its curves; one undo step).
- The curves' layer redraws when a solid carrying curves moves (a signature of those parts' transforms
  checked each frame) - G, the gizmo, a drag or typed numbers show the curves with it at once.
- No new member variables (locals / metas): hot reloads into an open editor.
- Docs: mesh-curves-procedural (positive / negative).

**Numbers:** test_negative_extrusions - a 1 x 1 x 0.4 block, a circle on top pushed 0.2 down: positive by
default (block whole, a new part); N: a 0.2-deep round pocket (0.4 - 0.04 pi x 0.2), the block's recipe a
live cut; the circle widened to r 0.3: the pocket follows; Make the cut positive: block whole + the disc as
its own part; Negative: cut again; undo. test_curves_redrawn_when_their_solid_moves.

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: every step editable any time (the recipe tree), roles, the CURVE box, no delays

**Asked:** an extrusion's properties available later, not a one-time thing - change existing extrudes and
other operations in real time whenever; change their roles (cutters, joiners...); everything live with no
delays; every property always accessible.

**Done (scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd):**
- The SOLID box shows the selected solid's whole **recipe** as a tree (`_fill_recipe` / `_recipe_rows`):
  each step's settings - extrusion height + **Both ways** (new: half each side of its curves' plane),
  revolve angle + steps, pipe radius - and each boolean step's **role** (Join / Cut / Common = union /
  difference / intersection) and **Separate** (`separate_node(path)`: the step becomes its first side, the
  tool solid a positive part again where it was - its place worked out down the path). Steps addressed by
  path (`node_at`, `with_node`); every change one undo step (`set_recipe`). The rows are rebuilt only when
  the recipe's shape changes (else just their values: a spin box keeps focus while typing).
- The **CURVE** box: the picked curve's name, a circle's radius, a line's corner radius, Closed - live,
  undoable; several picked: set on all that have it.
- No delays: live booleans are made again at once on every change (the 120 ms limit while dragging gone).
- All panel connections are methods with bound paths (hot reload safe); no new member variables.
- Docs: mesh-curves-procedural (the recipe, roles, Both ways, the CURVE box).

**Numbers:** test_recipe_tree_editable_any_time (a block cut by a cylinder: the block's height 0.4 -> 0.6
and the cut's depth 0.2 -> 0.4 inside the recipe; role Cut -> Join -> Common (the shared cylinder) -> Cut;
Both ways: half the cut in the block; undo x7 back; Separate), test_curve_box_properties_live (circle radius
0.2 -> 0.3: cylinder follows; corner radius, Closed, rename; undo).
- (Roles everywhere) The user didn't see roles: they're on boolean steps only, and their solid was one
  extrusion of two circles. Now: (1) every solid has a **Role** in the SOLID box - New solid (positive,
  default) / Cut / Join / Common with the solid it's in (`set_solid_role`: finds the solid it's in, makes
  the live boolean; switchable later in that solid's recipe). (2) An extrusion / fill of several curves lists
  each curve with **Add / Cut** (`_curve_role` -> the step's "roles" {id: add|cut}; `combined()` joins the
  added curves and takes the cut ones away (`curve_bool` with per-curve ops) before extruding - one clean
  closed solid, live). Test test_roles_for_every_solid_and_curve (two overlapping circles extruded: circle
  2 Cut -> circle 1 minus the lens, closed, within 2%; both Add -> one joined solid; undo; a cylinder in a
  block: Cut the solid it's in -> a live cut).
- (Ghosts) A cut solid left nothing to see. Now every solid inside a recipe (a boolean's B, nested too) is
  shown where it is as a see-through ghost - red cutting, green joined, blue common; unshaded, no depth test
  (seen through the solid), no shadow - in the view's world (never saved), made again when a recipe's key,
  a part's place or its showing changes (`ghost_sig` checked each frame -> `update_ghosts` / `_ghost_walk`).
  A **Ghosts** box (by Grid / Points) turns them off (a meta). Test test_ghosts_of_cut_solids (one red
  ghost of the cutter's shape, in the view not the model; Join -> green; off; separated -> none).
- (Ghosts, also for cut curves) The user saw no ghost: their cut was a curve's Cut role inside one
  extrusion, not a boolean step. Now each curve with the Cut role inside a step shows too - that curve
  made as the step would make it alone (its height, Both ways), red (`_ghost_walk` leaf branch,
  `_ghost_add`); every procedural part is watched for changes, not only booleans. Test
  test_ghosts_of_cut_curves.
- (Per-curve heights) Each curve in an extrusion step has its own **height** and **Both ways** (the step's
  till changed: "per": {id: {value, both}} - `_curve_value`, `_curve_both`; rows under each curve's role).
  `_extrude_step`: one height for all -> combined in 2D as before; heights of their own -> everything that
  adds (same-height ones joined in 2D, `_joined`) unioned first, then everything that cuts subtracted (3D,
  MeshBool) - the user found an added circle given a lower height of its own was no longer cut (it was
  unioned after the cuts). Cut curves' ghosts use their own height. Tests test_cut_curve_own_height (a 0.1
  deep pocket, its ghost 0.1, the block's own 0.6, undo), test_added_curve_own_height_still_cut.

## 2026-11-25 - Curve modeling: the OVERVIEW tree

**Asked:** an overview of the solids and curves (like the outliner of a 3D app) to select them and edit
them separately or together.

  round loop a circle, flat loops fitted as paths, others Douglas-Peucker polylines); `params` places each
  chain point along its curve. Recipe {kind: edges, ids, net, chains: [{id, pts, t}], c0: the curves as
  traced}; the mesh it was traced from kept per net (`_edge_bases`; after a load: the saved mesh).
  `edge_solid` / `EdgeNet.deform`: each chain point moved as its curve moved there (now - then, at its
  place along it), a corner the larger move, shaded again. A dragged point moves the same corner on the
  solid's other edges (`_move_corner`). Before a save `rebase_edges` makes the mesh and curves as they

- (2026-11-25, baked faces made from their edges; shading) Reported: shading issues on a baked solid after
  moving its edges (streaks, spikes). Causes: the mesh the bake traced came from a boolean - long thin
  triangles and points partway up walls on no edge; moving edges bent those triangles (folds), a circle's
  handle turned its points round (twist). Now: (1) a bake also records the mesh's faces (`EdgeNet.faces`:
  triangles grouped between the edges, the edge loops round each) - flat ones are filled again from their
  edge curves, a wall between two edges (four round it, two straight sides; or two rims) made again as a
  strip between those two, a band between two loops of edges likewise (`build`), anything else moved with
  its edges as before - so each edit makes the faces fresh from the curves; (2) a round edge moves its
  points by their angle round the centre (`_round_move`); (3) points on no edge follow their neighbours
  (`_spread`); (4) smooth shading weights faces by their angle at each corner, not their area (slivers
  don't skew it); the fallback faces' winding fixed (they came out inside out). The rebuild check also
  watches the recipe's faces. The user's solid given its faces: 10 flat, 2 strips, 1 band - smooth.
  Test test_baked_faces_made_from_edges (a cylinder's top rim widened: a frustum's volume).

- (2026-11-25, baked solids: an even mesh moved smoothly with its edges) Agreed plan: the shading and
  distortion came from the boolean's long thin triangles being bent. The bake now remeshes: `EdgeNet.remesh`
  (welded; long edges split longest first - an edge of the solid's halves stay on it - then flips toward
  wider angles across nearly flat edges and easing of points inside faces), triangles sized from the
  surface area (a few thousand: a cylinder 4.6k, the user's solid 2.7k; bake 0.35-0.75 s). The recipe keeps
  the mesh itself ({mesh: {v, t}}) and each edge point's chain and place along its curve (fv, in order
  along each chain). An edit (`_edge_mesh`): the edge points move as their curves moved
  (`edge_moves`; circles by angle), the points inside each face whose edges moved get a first guess
  blended from all its edge points (1 / distance^4, the nearest 400 - `blend_weights`, once per bake;
  faces split only at true edge segments) and are settled with over-relaxed neighbour averaging
  (`blend_moves`); faces whose edges didn't move stay still. ~50 ms an edit. Saving makes the mesh as
  it is and the curves as they are the new start. Checked in a window on a copy of the user's solid:
  a recess arc bent 10 cm - clean, smooth. Tests: test_bake_solid, test_baked_mesh_follows_its_edges_smoothly
  (a cylinder's top rim widened: a frustum within 4%, no folds).

  mesh, pulling a recess arc out (a wall strongly sheared) left its inside points lagging (teeth) and its

  faces; a wall's points (a face standing along the axis) move with the edge points straight below and
  above them, mixed by height (`_column`) - straight between its edges, not smoothed; flat faces are blended
  as before. And it's shaded by its faces (`EdgeNet.shaded`): every point's normal the angle-weighted blend
  of its own face's triangles - smooth across a face however its triangles lean, sharp only at the solid's
  edges. Checked in a window on a copy of the user's solid (their edits): clean walls, smooth shading.

  axis): the faces of the boolean's mesh found between its edges; the axis from the biggest flat face;
  each wall (a face standing along it) gets a footprint - its edges seen along the axis: the longest rail,

  triangles each; each wall checked (its edges along its footprint, no quads over each other) else it

  The solid's way up kept with it ("up") so walls are told apart for the move. The user's solid (their
  original re-baked): 2.5k triangles, every wall as quads; its recess arc pulled out 15 cm in a window -
  a clean, smooth slanted wall.

- (2026-11-25, walls smooth round a bent side edge; Smooth / Sharp point) Reported: the geometry distorted
  (after pulling out a side edge and reshaping the recess's arcs: lumpy, blotchy walls); asked: a
  right-click entry to make a point smooth or sharp. The walls' side-edge bends had been blended in by
  1 / d^4 weights (flat spots - lumps); now a wall's points sit straight between their rails plus an
  offset settled smooth over the wall's grid (each point's offset the over-relaxed average of its
  neighbours', the rails' offsets none, the side edges' as they bend) - an even stretch between all its
  edges. ~50 ms an edit on the user's solid. The right-click menu on a picked curve's point (first row
  of its Curve modeling page): Smooth point / Sharp point - the curve becomes a path (a line: every point
  sharp; a spline: every point smooth; an arc: as points on it) with that point's mark set; one undo
  step; new icons m_cv_pt_smooth / m_cv_pt_sharp. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (_blend's wall
  columns, blend_moves), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (point_items, point_sharp, set_point_sharp,
  menu_groups(at)), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (menu passes where it was opened),
  scripts/editor/mesh/curve_icons.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (test_point_smooth_or_sharp_menu),
  data/docs/editor.md.
- (2026-11-25, double-click a point dissolves it) Asked: double-clicking an existing point should dissolve
  it. A double-click on a picked curve's point takes it out (`dissolve_point`): the curve runs on between
  its neighbours (its smooth / sharp mark and corner radius go with it); an arc's middle point leaves a
  straight line; not when too few would be left (2 open, 3 closed) nor a baked solid's edge end (a corner
  other edges share). One undo step. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (view_input,
  dissolve_point), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (test_double_click_dissolves_point), data/docs/editor.md.
- (2026-11-25, baked walls built right at steps and notches) Reported: editing a baked side edge, the
  geometry didn't follow the curve. Two faults in the bake's wall builder (`EdgeNet.quad_mesh`): a column
  ran from the lowest edge at its spot to the highest - straight across a hole or notch in the wall
  (a block with a recess, built along the "wrong" one of equal axes, came out with the recess filled:
  volume 1.027 vs 0.96); and at a step (a recess's side) the tall column's rows were joined to the short
  one's row for row - zero-width slivers from the edge's points up into the wall above, which stretched
  into spikes and dragged that wall once the edge moved. Now each column is every stretch between two edge
  crossings that lies on the face (the face's triangles laid flat - along it, up it - tell), rows are at
  heights the whole wall shares (every L and every column's end; points welded, so walls either side of
  an edge share them), and neighbouring columns are zipped only over the heights they share (quads where
  rows match, a triangle where one goes on). Also the faces of a baked mesh are told apart by its own
  edges lying along a curve (`EdgeNet.feature_edges`), not by consecutive edge points (which, with each
  wall's own points on an edge, paired points of different walls and merged the faces). The user's solid
  (made with the old builder) re-baked from their original solids, their edits (three edges) put back
  as one step: 1970 triangles, 31 edges, an edit ~40-55 ms. Tests: test_baked_recess_side_edge_stays_in_its_walls
  (the recess kept: same volume; the wall above it stays put when its side edge bends; the edge's middle
  goes out with it). Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (quad_mesh, _columns_at, _on_face2,
  feature_edges), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (_edge_mesh), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd.
- (2026-11-25, smooth smart dragging of curve points and curves) Asked: points jumped around when moved;
  wanted smart movement that takes the view into account, easy along X / Y / Z - and no snapping, smooth
  and fluid. Dragging a point (or a picked curve) is now measured from where it was pressed (no jump to
  under the mouse), still for the first 6 px, then - Smart axis move (the editor's move mode) - along
  the model's X, Y or Z, whichever runs closest to the drag on screen (an axis pointing at the camera
  skipped); the axis drawn through it in its colour with the distance by the mouse; X / Y / Z switch
  axis (again: free on the axis plane facing the view most squarely); Shift at the start or Perspective
  move: free on that plane. No snapping (to the grid or to points) - smooth; Ctrl: whole grid steps
  from the start. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (_drag_delta, _line_t, _axis_on_screen,
  _facing_axis, _drag_hint, _drag_to, _draw_drag, key, view_input), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd
  (test_point_drag_smart_axis), data/docs/editor.md.
- (2026-11-25, guides while dragging) Asked: auto snapping with guides shown in the view - to the level
  of another point of the same curve, of a flat area, etc. While a point (or a curve) is dragged, each
  axis it's free to move along (the locked axis, or the two of the plane) snaps to the nearest level
  within 8 px on screen: another point's X / Y / Z (its own curve's first, then any curve's), or a flat
  face's level (the visible parts' faces square to an axis, gathered once a drag); a dashed guide in the
  axis's colour from what it lines up with (a face: a level line through the point) and a note ("Y
  same as a point on this curve", "Y level with a flat face"). The Guides box (by Points; a meta, on by
  default); Alt while dragging: off; Ctrl (grid steps): no guides. Files:
  scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (guides_on, _guide_levels, _apply_guides, _draw_drag, the Guides
  box), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (test_point_drag_guides), data/docs/editor.md.
- (2026-11-26, baked solids: quad flat faces, closed meshes) Reported: shading / geometry distortion on a
  flat face after its edge was pushed (a crease); asked: avoid triangles, quads as much as possible.
  The flat faces of a baked solid (those square to its way up - tops, bottoms, a recess's ceiling) are
  now built of quads like its walls (`EdgeNet.quad_caps`, once a solid, flag "qcaps"): columns across
  the face along its longest straight edge - at the rim's points (every point where the rim turns back,
  the others not closer than L/3) and every L - each from rim to rim (a point where the face narrows to
  a corner: its wedge fanned), rows at heights the face shares (welded where two columns meet), columns
  zipped row to row (quads), each strip's ends taking the rim points between its columns; a column's end
  between two rim points is a new point on that edge, the wall beyond split there too. A flat face moves
  like a wall: each point between its column's two rim ends (the direction read off its grid). Walls'
  rows now at heights the whole solid shares, so walls meeting at an edge share their points; the mesh
  closed where two sides still differ (`close_seams`: duplicates welded, an edge split at the other
  side's points - flag "sealed"); flat-face slivers along a gently curved edge joined to their face.
  After each move, triangles turned over are untangled (inner points eased; an edge flipped as a last
  resort - drawing only). Also fixed: `tie_edges` changed a packed array passed in (copied in Godot)
  so its welds never reached the triangles - it returns them now. The user's solid re-baked from their
  originals (asked; edits on 6 edges re-applied as one step): 3478 triangles, closed (0 open edges).
  Known: a very large edit (an arc's middle moved ~40 cm) still bends the faces near it unevenly.
  Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (quad_caps, _cap_grid, _along_chain, _cap_columns, untangle,
  flip_fix, close_seams, tie_edges, quad_mesh's shared levels, _blend's flat faces), curve_tools.gd
  (_edge_mesh's one-time passes), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (test_baked_flat_face_follows_without_folding,
  the recess test's closed-mesh check).
- (2026-11-26, baked solids settle when an edit's let go; wireframe) Asked: rebuild-on-release; areas
  needing more polygons subdivided, quads kept; a wireframe display to spot problems. Settling
  (`EdgeNet.settle`, `settle_edges` from `_changed` - each edit's end): the edge points spread evenly
  along their curves between the corners, the inner points relaxed along the surface (no fold, shape
  kept), then that's the solid's new start (its mesh, its edge points, c0 = its curves now) - ~0.3-0.5 s;
  the movement weights for the next drag worked out on a worker meanwhile (waited for when a drag
  starts or the tools close). Undo keeps the baked solids' recipes too (`_state`), so it puts the mesh
  back exactly. Local subdivision of bent patches (quads into four quads, new points on the curved
  surface, the patch's border points straight, the triangles beyond fanned) is written but switched
  off (max_deg 180) - on the user's creased solid it split too much and was slow. Found and fixed on
  the way: strip triangles along curved rims made inside out (now turned by the rim's direction), and
  `EdgeNet.orient` turns a whole closed mesh outwards (once a solid, flag "oriented") - the dark notches.
  Wireframe: the mesh editor toolbar's Wireframe button / Shift+W - the parts' edges over them in object
  mode, quads as quads (diagonals left out), hidden lines hidden (`update_wire`, a meta - hot reload
  safe). The user's solid: closed, consistently turned (0 open edges, 0 inside out). Files:
  scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (settle, _split_bent, _edge_inside, _feat_now, face_of, orient,
  _cap_grid's rim strips), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (_state/_set_state, _changed,
  settle_edges, _edge_mesh's background weights, _exit_tree), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (wireframe),
  tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (test_edit_settles_baked_mesh_and_wireframe), data/docs/editor.md.
- (2026-11-26, smooth solve, loop cuts, cleaner quads) Asked: improve the bending for large edits and
  turn subdivision back on with creases told from curvature - finish everything. The baked mesh's
  movement is now solved by conjugate gradients (`EdgeNet.cg_setup` / `cg_moves`, cotangent weights on
  the mesh as made, Jacobi-preconditioned): a wall's or flat face's points straight between their
  rails plus the side edges' bends spread smooth over it, other faces spread from their edges; a drag
  goes on from the last frame's solution (40 rounds a frame, ~37 ms on the user's solid), letting go
  solves it fully (~1 s) before settling. Settling no longer re-spaces or relaxes points (that skewed
  the columns). Subdivision is now loop cuts (`_split_bent`): where neighbouring quads bend over 25°,
  the strips beside that edge cut - each quad in two (four where cuts cross), carried quad to quad
  across the solid till it closes or meets a triangle; new points on the curved surface, on the curve
  on a solid's edge; skipped when bends are everywhere (creases). Found: rim edges of a face could be
  missed as the solid's edges, merging a wall with the top beside it - `feature_edges` now also counts
  any edge where faces meet over 45°. Strip-end fans along rims fanned from the new point (no
  three-in-a-line slivers). Wireframe: a bent quad still drawn as a quad. The user's shape (their
  originals baked, their edits as one, settled): closed, every triangle facing out, 87% of triangles in
  quads, settle 0.44 s. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (cg_setup, cg_moves, _split_bent,
  feature_edges, settle; blend_moves removed), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (_edge_mesh,
  settle_edges), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (wireframe), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (settle test:
  facing out, 80%+ quads), data/docs/editor.md.

  game when its toolbar lacks it (`_ensure_wire_button` - a toolbar built before a live update added
  the button gets it at once). File: scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd.

- (2026-11-26, baked solids shaded by angle; seams and loop cuts kept off the walls) Reported: shading
  issues and random triangles on the baked solid. Its shading had been by faces flooded between its
  edges; a face whose flood crossed into the wall beside it (through the strips along a reshaped rim)
  averaged the top's normals with the wall's - the staircase streaks. Now each corner's normal is the
  blend of the triangles round its point facing within 40° of its own (`EdgeNet.shaded`): smooth across
  curves, sharp at every real edge, whatever the face grouping. On the user's shape: shading normals off
  their triangle by 45° or more 513 -> 0 corners. Also: `close_seams` takes a point onto another side's
  edge loosely (a curved edge's chord) only when it lies on the same curve as both ends - not a wall's
  point just under a rim; loop cuts put a new point on a curve only when both ends share it, and bow
  points out onto the curved surface only away from the edges; the smooth solve's moves get six light
  smoothing rounds (where two runs of columns meet at a step). Known: a short wall between a reshaped
  edge and its rim (the user's edge 7 band) keeps long skewed quads. Files:
  scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (shaded, close_seams, _split_bent, cg_moves).
- (2026-11-26, settling straightens the walls' columns) Asked: keep working on the shading issues. When
  an edit settles, `EdgeNet.straighten_columns` slides each point of a reshaped edge that ends a wall's
  column (one rising along the solid's way up, however it leans - flat faces' columns excluded; a strip
  too short for inner points: its triangles' sides from edge to edge) to the place on its curve nearest
  the column's other end (corners not counted as partners), kept in order between the edge's corners;
  the points up each such column put back on the line between its ends. Measured on the user's shape
  (fresh bake + their six edits): closed, shading within 30°. Known: where an edit stretches one edge of
  a wall much longer than the edge facing it (the user's edge 7 band, pulled ~30 cm out under a fixed
  rim) the wall keeps its column count, so its columns fan out - fixing that needs the face's grid
  rebuilt for its new shape. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (straighten_columns),
  scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (settle_edges).
- (2026-11-26, settling rebuilds four-sided faces at a reshaped edge) Asked: rebuild stretched faces
  (the fanning). When an edit settles, each face (between the solid's edges) that touches a reshaped edge
  and is bounded by one loop with four corners is made again (`EdgeNet._rebuild_faces`): its two longer
  sides the rails, a column at every point either rail has (the other rail's point at nearly the same
  share paired with it, else a new point there on its curve - the faces beyond meet it through
  close_seams), and every L along the longer rail; rows from its two other sides; points inside by a
  Coons patch of its four sides (its bends kept); zipped column to column, quads where rows match. Kept
  only when the whole mesh stays closed (else settled as before). Checked: a block's top corner pulled
  0.6 m out - its two walls rebuilt as straight leaning columns (no fan), closed; the user's shape (fresh
  bake + their edits): rebuilt and closed, shading within 30°. Not covered: a face that isn't four-sided -
  the user's edge-7 band is part of the cylinder's whole wall (one face round it, cut by the recess), so
  it keeps the straightened columns. Files: scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (_rebuild_faces,
  _open_edges, settle), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (settle_edges), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd
  (test_settle_rebuilds_stretched_walls).
